title: Remove the BUILTINS and MACHINES tables and the compiled-in file copy from posting_files.rs: the folders are the only source

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this on 2026-11-20, after he saw that `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` still has the embedded lists:

> So why is the "embedded" list still in the system.. that should have been removed and the mch files instead read from assets folder, populated from disk.

Now (main at 13f26da99):
- #2282 removed the compiled-in files from the desktop build. The desktop reads `assets/posts` and `assets/machines` at run time.
- #2414 made the displayed lists follow the folders. A file with no table entry is listed as a file entry.
- But the fixed tables `BUILTINS` (line 36) and `MACHINES` (line 77) remain. They map a registry name to a file name. `builtin_post_text` and `builtin_machine_text` read a built-in by registry name. Entry 0 of `BUILTINS` must stay Fanuc.
- The function behind `#[cfg(any(target_arch = "wasm32", test))]` (from line 323) holds 63 `include_str!` lines. The browser build and the tests use this copy.
- `posting_files.rs` is 406 lines. The limit is about 400.

Wanted:
- The folders are the only source of the post list and the machine list. A new file in the folder is a complete entry. No Rust change is needed to add a machine or a post.
- Each file states its own display name. The name, the sort order and the default role come from the file or from a small index file in the folder. Choose one design in the decision file.
- The `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` tables are deleted.
- A project that names a built-in post or machine by its old registry name still opens. Keep a small, documented alias map for the old names only (`PostRef::Builtin` and the default document's post must still resolve). No saved project changes meaning.
- The browser build gets its files without the `include_str!` list: a generated manifest, or files that the page fetches. If this is too large, split it out as a sub-issue and keep the list for the browser build only.
- Tests read the same folders. They do not use the compiled-in copy.

Open questions for the work:
- Where the display name and the order live for a file that has no header.
- What the golden tests and `PostRef::Builtin` need to stay unchanged.
- How the release package and the dev tree find the folders (`camcraft_post::data_dir`).

Safety:
- This can change which post a project posts with. A wrong post means wrong G-code. The work needs a test that every old registry name resolves to the same file as before, and a refusal by name for a missing file.
- `effort:high` by the safety floor.

Done means: `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` are gone. Adding a `.mch` or `.cps` file to the folder shows it in the list with no code change. Every old registry name still resolves to the same file. `posting_files.rs` is under 400 lines. The `include_str!` copy is gone, or is limited to the browser build with its own sub-issue.

Related: #2282 (closed), #2414 (merged), #2500 (follow-up).
